nodes.name: Fetch Launch Record
nodes.notes: Launch row contract (ruled 2026-09-02): Client, Table (must be "Companies", by name, no default), View (by name, required, no default), Sources, Departments, Max companies. Launch Params refuses anything else before a paid call.

nodes.name: Sub Trigger
nodes.notes: Event entry: one item carrying the same keys as a launch row (Client, Table, View, Tag, and Domains for the insert doors). This is how an insert door calls this machine after landing: Table "Companies", View "Not Sourced", Domains = what it landed. No launch row, no Running stamp; Stamp Progress creates the run row on Execution ID after the first pass.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Event-Row.js

nodes.name: Resolve Base
nodes.notes: A launch row with no Client link used to kill the run right here: $json.fields.Client[0] threw inside the node before Launch Params could name the refusal, so the row got nothing back. It now asks for "recMISSING" and keeps going; Launch Params reads the answer defensively and refuses with the reason.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Launch-Params.js

nodes.name: Launch OK?
nodes.notes: The refusal gate. Launch Params names a bad launch row instead of throwing; false here means refused, and Build Refusal closes the row as Failed with the reason before anything is read or paid for.

nodes.name: Stamp Running
nodes.notes: First thing the launch door does, ahead of every guard: the row carries the Execution ID and link from the moment the POST lands, so a refusal or a crash can always be read back on the row the Operator launched. It passes the record through, so Resolve Base still reads fields.Client off it.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Find-Tables.js

nodes.name: Read Companies View
nodes.notes: The Companies view (by name, required on the launch row) is the selector; Max companies (required) is the read limit and the spend cap. A view that does not exist crashes here, before any paid call, into the Error Logger. Tag is not read: People stores none.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Pick-Companies.js
@@file:nodes/People-Filters.js

nodes.name: Read People
nodes.notes: Tier zero: what the base already holds at these domains, ids only, one call per 100 domains. Domain on People is a lookup through the Companies link; the {Domain} filter matches the lookup's text and the field comes back as an array of one.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Make-Batches.js

nodes.name: Loop Batches
nodes.notes: The writer lane: one 250-company batch per sub-execution, one after another (Airtable's 5 requests per second per base is a global ceiling, so parallel identical lanes buy nothing; measured 2026-09-02). Its done output ends the writer lane and hands every closed batch to the AI-Ark lane.

nodes.name: Run Batch
nodes.notes: Mode writer, awaited: ContaGen and Supersoniq for the batch, Clean Fields, DNC, the People writer (PATCH in tens), the Companies stamps, a recount, then its own Hub row keyed <this execution>-<batchNum>, and its counters plus the recount's held state back as the last node's output (the held state feeds this batch's AI-Ark pass). A crash comes back as an error item and is logged; never retried (the paid tiers would run twice).

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Pass-Result.js

nodes.name: AT List Views
nodes.notes: After every writer batch and after the AI-Ark lane's row (ruled 2026-09-02): read the base meta again; the email door fires only if People carries a view named exactly "Not Waterfalled".

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Find-Waterfall-View.js

nodes.name: Fire Waterfall
nodes.notes: The one email hand-off, after the last batch: Enrich Emails record door, People view Not Waterfalled (repointed from Waterfall Emails 2026-09-09).

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Handoff-Tick.js

nodes.name: Stamp Progress
nodes.notes: Live Running row after every hand-off, on the launch row's Execution ID (created here on an event run). Write-only progress from this execution's own memory; no Tally, no read-add-write. The counters live in the pass rows and are summed at the close.

nodes.name: Stop?
nodes.notes: True when the batch had every paid call fail after retry: the paid tiers are dead, launching more batches would only burn time. The ark passes already fired keep running; the close waits for their rows.

nodes.name: Read Batch Rows
nodes.notes: At the close: the pass rows of this run, by prefix (Execution ID "<this execution>-<batchNum>" and "<this execution>-<batchNum>-ark", Automation "Waterfall Contacts Batch"). Each row's Tally is that pass's counters; Build Log sums them. A failed read crashes loudly rather than logging zeros.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Build-Log.js
@@file:nodes/Build-Refusal.js

nodes.name: Build Refusal
nodes.notes: A badly filled launch row closes here as Failed with the named reason and the execution link, on the same row Stamp Running opened. Refusals are expected outcomes and are logged as such; the Error Logger still owns real crashes.

nodes.name: Legacy Door
nodes.notes: The old door the per-machine Airtable automation still POSTs. Delete once the single Launch automation posts to /webhook/enrich-contacts.
